title: Fluid Flow
sourceLocation: Owner's ChatGPT Library (original master remains outside public GitHub)
sourceScope: Streamline/laminar and turbulent flow, incompressible and non-viscous assumptions of an ideal fluid; simple flow-rate Q = V/t and unit conversions. Continuity equation belongs to Topic 6.4.
importantDistinction: The source uses 'steady (streamline or laminar)' at introductory level; real fluid mechanics distinguishes steady (time dependence) from laminar (flow regime). Do not imply universal equivalence. Irrotational also does not imply straight particle paths.
limitations: All 80 original stems/options/answers/explanations preserved with line wrapping normalized.
The original figure-dependent MCQs have been visually verified against the NBF printed figures and now render V90 independent educational drawings in public practice; no NBF scans are published.
20 source situation/scenario-labelled items are independent standalone questions, not any common-stimulus group. 19 selectable after Q80 hold.
FBISE framework marks SLO P-11-B-35 Summative with Knowledge + Understanding topic cognitive level; no individual source question is independently certified.
Source flow-rate Q=V/t exercises are supporting basic numeracy, not an extra specified FBISE B-35 assessment requirement.
This is PUBLIC provisional self-practice only, not a secure exam or official board paper. No saved cloud grade.
Central Test Builder remains V79 with 1,846 selectable MCQs until later verified integration; complete Unit6 course stays planned.

questions.stem: Which description best identifies a fluid?

options.text: A substance that can flow, such as a liquid or gas
A substance that must keep a fixed shape
Only a liquid that flows through a pipe

questions.explanation: A substance that can flow, such as a liquid or gas. The textbook includes both liquids and gases in the category of fluids.

questions.stem: In Topic 6.3, the flow rate of a fluid is defined as the:

options.text: Volume passing a point per unit time
Distance travelled by one molecule per second

questions.explanation: Volume passing a point per unit time. Volumetric flow rate is volume divided by the time taken.

questions.stem: Why can two streamline paths not cross at the same point in a steady velocity field?

options.text: A single point cannot have two distinct velocity directions at once
Fluid particles cannot exist inside a pipe bend
Pressure would have to become exactly zero
The fluid would immediately become a solid

questions.explanation: A single point cannot have two distinct velocity directions at once. At one point, a defined velocity vector has a unique direction.

questions.explanation: Viscosity accounts for internal resistance omitted from the ideal model. The distinguishing idealization is zero viscosity; real fluids resist relative motion.
